learnables.predictableError: the body part is the SUBJECT and stays nominative — 'Boli me glava', never 'boli me glavo'; the person is the accusative clitic 'me', not a possessive ('moja glava boli'). Two or more parts flip the verb: 'Bolijo me noge.'
in 'Boli me glava' it is the subject in the nominative — the slip is the accusative 'boli me glavo' on the English 'my head' model
'trebuh' is the belly you point at; 'želodec' is the stomach organ — for a stomach ache you say 'Boli me trebuh'
it is neuter — 'vneto grlo' (a sore throat), not 'vnet grlo'
the nominative plural is irregular 'zobje' (not 'zobi'), and two or more flip the verb — 'Bolijo me zobje'; one aching tooth is just 'Boli me zob'
the person is the dative clitic 'mi' — 'Slabo mi je', not 'Sem slab'; and it means nauseous/faint, not 'I feel bad' in general, which is 'Slabo se počutim'
'I have a fever' takes the accusative — 'Imam vročino', not 'imam vročina'

Slovenes say 'Prehlajen sem. / Prehlajena sem.' — participle first, since 'sem' is a second-position clitic; the calque 'Imam prehlad.' is said but noticeably less idiomatic. A cold is not 'gripa' (flu).
'to the doctor' is 'k' + DATIVE — 'grem k zdravniku', not 'k zdravnik'
the same word means 'recipe' — at the pharmacy the distinction is 'na recept' (on prescription) vs 'brez recepta' (over the counter)
you normally ask in the plural — 'tablete proti bolečinam'; accusative singular is 'tableto' and 'pet tablet' is the genitive plural
'by train' is 'z' + INSTRUMENTAL — 'z vlakom', not 'z vlak'; and 'na vlak' (boarding) vs 'na vlaku' (aboard)
accusative 'vozovnico' — 'Eno vozovnico, prosim'; at a ticket window locals very often just say 'karta' ('Eno karto do Maribora, prosim'), and a cinema or museum ticket is 'vstopnica'
'on platform 2' is the locative 'na drugem peronu'; note Slovenian station announcements usually say 'tir' (track), not 'peron'
'odhod' (od- = away) is departure and 'prihod' (pri- = towards) is arrival — the prefix is the whole difference on a board
mirror of 'odhod' — beginners read the two off a board by the shared '-hod' and pick the wrong column
it is a feminine SINGULAR mass noun covering all your bags — 'moja prtljaga je težka', not an English-style plural; 'prtljage' is the genitive singular ('nimam prtljage'), not 'bags'
the stem gains a -j- when it declines — 's taksijem' (by taxi), 'v taksiju' — not 'z taksi'
masculine even though it ends in -o, like 'kino' — 'z avtom', 'v avtu'; beginners decline it as a neuter

learnables.gloss: by ___ / with ___ — the means: 'z avtom', 'z vlakom', 's taksijem'
learnables.predictableError: the means takes the INSTRUMENTAL ('z avtom', not 'z avto'), and the preposition is 's' before a voiceless consonant ('s taksijem', 's kartico') but 'z' elsewhere
accusative 'rezervacijo' — 'Imam rezervacijo'; it is the noun, and it cannot stand in for the verb 'rezervirati'
'the room key' is 'ključ od sobe' — genitive after 'od'; and it is inanimate, so the accusative equals the nominative ('dobim ključ')
'noč' is feminine and its dual is 'dve noči' — not 'dva noči' or 'dve noč'
the sign is the neuter 'Odprto'; describing the shop the adjective agrees — 'trgovina je odprta' — and asking a person is 'Ali ste odprti?'
the sign is the neuter 'Zaprto'; with a noun it agrees — 'trgovina je zaprta', 'muzej je zaprt'
on its own the sign is the neuter 'Prepovedano', but attached to a noun it agrees — 'Vstop prepovedan', 'Kajenje prepovedano'
'vstop' is entry as an act — the doorway itself is 'vhod'; the sign reads 'Vstop prepovedan', 'Vstop prost'
confusing 'izhod' (the door out) with 'odhod' (a departure time); the emergency exit is 'izhod v sili'
the printed word is the bare noun 'Pozor!'; the spoken warning to a person is the verb 'Pazi!' / 'Pazite!'
the desk is always the plural 'Informacije'; a single piece of information is the singular 'informacija' ('Hvala za informacijo.')

learnables.gloss: opening hours (of a shop, a museum)
learnables.predictableError: the phrase is masculine — 'kakšen je odpiralni čas', not 'kakšni'; 'odpiralni čas' is the shop-door wording, and you will just as often see 'delovni čas' on the same door
a percentage takes the GENITIVE — '20 % popusta', 'popust na vse' — not '20 % popust'
'cena' is the printed price; across a counter Slovenes ask 'Koliko stane?', not the stiff 'Kakšna je cena?'
'delo' is work in general ('iščem delo'); the paid post you actually hold is 'služba' ('imam novo službo') — English 'job' maps to both

learnables.gloss: We are looking for ___. (the job-ad frame)
learnables.predictableError: the object goes accusative, and an animate masculine takes -a — 'Iščemo natakarja', not 'Iščemo natakar'

learnables.gloss: For rent / to let: I let out ___. (as written by a private owner; an agency writes 'Oddamo')
learnables.predictableError: English 'rent' goes both ways — 'oddam' is the owner letting it out ('Oddam stanovanje'), while renting FROM someone is 'najamem'; and the next card along reading 'PRODAM' is for SALE, not for rent.
'a Slovene course' is the genitive 'tečaj slovenščine', and you attend it with 'na' + accusative — 'hodim na tečaj'; the same word also means exchange rate
'prijava' is the noun on the notice ('Prijave zbiramo do 10. septembra'); signing yourself up is the verb 'prijavim se' — the noun cannot stand in for it

learnables.gloss: Yesterday I ___ed — the past tense: the -l participle + 'sem'
learnables.predictableError: the participle agrees with the SPEAKER'S gender — a man says 'Včeraj sem bil', a woman 'Včeraj sem bila' — and 'sem' alone carries the past; there is no second auxiliary to add

learnables.sl: Bil sem doma. / Bila sem doma.
learnables.predictableError: the past of 'biti' is the participle 'bil/bila' PLUS 'sem' — dropping 'sem' ('jaz bil doma') leaves no tense at all
the participle of 'iti' is suppletive — 'šel / šla', nothing like the infinitive; there is no regular form to build
it is the written (and phone) sign-off — walking out of a shop you say 'Nasvidenje', not 'Lep pozdrav'
'za' takes the ACCUSATIVE — 'Hvala za pomoč', 'Hvala za vabilo' — not the dative 'hvala pomoči' on the English 'thanks to' model
the reflexive 'se' is obligatory and what follows goes GENITIVE — 'Veselim se srečanja'; and it is not 'Me veseli', which is 'nice to meet you'
'hčerka' declines regularly — 'imam hčerko', 'dve hčerki' — while the standard 'hči' does not: its accusative is 'hčer' and its plural 'hčere'. It is not a diminutive; that is 'hčerkica'.
